newsitem.title: UK: Best of politicians' quotes on UK election outcome.
newsitem.headline: Best of politicians' quotes on UK election outcome.

text.p: Following is a selection of political reactions to the unfolding British election result on Tuesday morning, when the opposition Labour party seized an unprecedented victory and the Conservatives a humiliating defeat.
LABOUR LEADER TONY BLAIR ON VICTORY
"A new dawn has broken, has it not? We always said that if we had the courage to change then we could do it. And we did it.
"The British people have put their trust in us. It is a moving and a humbling experience and the size of our likely majority now imposes a special sort of responsibility upon us."
"We have been elected as New Labour and we will govern as New Labour. We were elected because as a party today we represent the whole of this nation and we will govern for the whole of this nation."
BLAIR AFTER HIS RE-ELECTION IN SEDGEFIELD
"I feel this evening a deep sense of honour, a deep sense of responsibility and a deep sense of humility. You have put your trust in me and I intend to repay that trust. I will not let you down."
CONSERVATIVE LEADER JOHN MAJOR ON DEFEAT
"Tonight we have been comprehensively defeated.

"We will listen to the voice of the electorate. We will consider what has been said to us... I know that when we have reflected we will begin to prepare once again for that day in the future -- I hope not too far distant -- when my party may once again return to government in the service of this country.

"The Labour party has had an extremely successful evening. I telephoned Mr Blair a little over an hour ago to congratulate him on his success and to wish him every good fortune in the great responsibilities that he will have in the years that lie ahead.
"This is a great country. He inherits a country in extremely good economic shape. I wish him every success in sustaining that in the interests of all the people of this country."
NEIL KINNOCK, FORMER LABOUR PARTY LEADER WHO LOST THE 1992 GENERAL ELECTION
"1992 was a time of mourning...today is literally a new dawn."
PETER MANDELSON, LABOUR CAMPAIGN MANAGER
"We've come back from the dead. We're alive, invigorated, a new, reborn party. That's what this election has been all about."
BRIAN MAWHINNEY, CONSERVATIVE PARTY CHAIRMAN
"The British people decided it was time for a change despite the fact we have some of the best economic news this country has seen for a couple of generations."
DAVID MELLOR after losing his Conservative seat to Labour in Putney
"A tidal wave was bursting over the Conservative party tonight. It wasn't a question of putting your hand in the dyke. It was a case of the sea wall collapsing all around you."
MICHAEL PORTILLO, DEFENCE SECRETARY after losing his seat to Labour

"A truly terrible night for the Conservatives. I would have wished to have been part of rebuilding it in the House of Commons but would like to do whatever I can from the wings to help rebuild a great party which has a great future."
FORMER WAR CORRESPONDENT MARTIN BELL after winning northwest England seat of Tatton on an anti-sleaze ticket
"What you have accomplished here is some kind of political miracle." Quoting English writer G.K. Chesterton, he added in his acceptance speech,
"'Smile at us, pay us, pass us but do not quite forget//
That we are the people of England and we have not spoken yet.'"
KENNETH CLARKE, CHANCELLOR OF THE EXCHEQUER after holding his central England seat for the Conservatives
"It looks ever more likely that we have lost and that the end of 18 years of very successful Conservative government have come.

"There has been far too little about the economy in this election and far too much about Europe...Had we had more on the economy, less on Europe and a lot less on sleaze, we would have done a lot better."
"I do think the party needs to compose itself, lose with dignity."
EDWINA CURRIE, FORMER CONSERVATIVE CABINET MEMBER
"It is clear that going Eurosceptic did not help the Conservatives one jot. A large number of Conservatives have simply switched to Labour."
THERESA GORMAN, MP FOR BILLERICAY AND A LEADING EUROSCEPTIC
"Our policies have not been what the Conservative voters in the country wanted. On the doorsteps in my constituency people said they were going to support me because of my views on Europe."
PADDY ASHDOWN, LEADER, LIBERAL DEMOCRATS

"There will be a hugely increased number of Liberal Democrats in parliament.(They will) fight...for the issues in this election -- investing in education, tackling the crisis in the health service, bringing a new kind of honesty to our politics."
MICHAEL HESELTINE, DEPUTY PRIME MINISTER
"We will be back."
